struct Vector2D
  getter x : Float64
  getter y : Float64

  def initialize(@x : Float64, @y : Float64)
  end

  def +(other : Vector2D) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x + other.x, @y + other.y)
  end

  def -(other : Vector2D) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x - other.x, @y - other.y)
  end

  def *(scalar : Float64) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x * scalar, @y * scalar)
  end

  def magnitude : Float64
    Math.sqrt(@x ** 2 + @y ** 2)
  end

  def normalize : Vector2D
    m = magnitude
    raise ArgumentError.new("cannot normalize a zero vector") if m == 0.0
    Vector2D.new(@x / m, @y / m)
  end

  def ==(other : Vector2D) : Bool
    @x == other.x && @y == other.y
  end
end

prompt: Write a Crystal class `AppCLI` with a class method `run(argv, io, err)` returning `Int32`. It should handle three subcommands — `start`, `stop`, and `status` — each dispatching to a private class method. The `start` subcommand accepts `--port N` (default 4000) and `--daemon` flag; `stop` and `status` take no flags. Unknown subcommands and `--help`/`-h` at the top level should print usage. All subcommand OptionParser instances must call `invalid_option` to reject unknown flags and return exit code 1.
completion:
require "option_parser"

class AppCLI
  USAGE = <<-USAGE
  Usage:
    app start [--port N] [--daemon]
    app stop
    app status
    app --help
  USAGE

  def self.run(argv : Array(String), io : IO = STDOUT, err : IO = STDERR) : Int32
    sub = argv.first?
    case sub
    when "start"  then start(argv[1..], io, err)
    when "stop"   then stop(argv[1..], io, err)
    when "status" then status(argv[1..], io, err)
    when "-h", "--help", nil
      io.puts USAGE
      0
    else
      err.puts "error: unknown subcommand: #{sub}"
      err.puts USAGE
      1
    end
  end

  private def self.start(args : Array(String), io : IO, err : IO) : Int32
    port = 4000
    daemon = false

    parser = OptionParser.new do |p|
      p.banner = "Usage: app start [--port N] [--daemon]"
      p.on("--port N", "Port to listen on (default: 4000)") { |v| port = v.to_i }
      p.on("--daemon", "Run in background") { daemon = true }
      p.on("-h", "--help", "Show help") { io.puts p; exit }
      p.invalid_option { |flag| err.puts "error: unknown flag: #{flag}"; exit 1 }
    end
    parser.parse(args)

    io.puts "Starting on port #{port}#{daemon ? " (daemon)" : ""}"
    0
  end

  private def self.stop(args : Array(String), io : IO, err : IO) : Int32
    OptionParser.parse(args) do |p|
      p.invalid_option { |flag| err.puts "error: unknown flag: #{flag}"; exit 1 }
    end
    io.puts "Stopping service"
    0
  end

  private def self.status(args : Array(String), io : IO, err : IO) : Int32
    OptionParser.parse(args) do |p|
      p.invalid_option { |flag| err.puts "error: unknown flag: #{flag}"; exit 1 }
    end
    io.puts "Service status: running"
    0
  end
end

exit AppCLI.run(ARGV)

class Pipeline
  def run(n : Int32) : Array(Int32)
    channel = Channel(Int32).new(capacity: 16)
    results = [] of Int32
    done = Channel(Nil).new

    spawn do
      n.times { |i| channel.send(i + 1) }
      channel.close
    end

    spawn do
      while (v = channel.receive?)
        results << v ** 2
      end
      done.send(nil)
    end

    done.receive

  end

require "channel"

def fan_out(source : Channel(String), workers : Int32) : Channel(String)
  output = Channel(String).new(capacity: workers * 4)

  workers.times do
    spawn do
      while (msg = source.receive?)
        output.send(msg.upcase)
      end
    end
  end

  spawn do
    # drain tracker: reuse a counting channel to know when all workers are done
    # Workers share source; close output after all finish via a separate latch
    latch = Channel(Nil).new
    workers.times { latch.receive }
    output.close
  end

  output
end

Write a top-level `parallel_map(items : Array(T), workers : Int32, &block : T -> R) : Array(R) forall T, R` that processes items concurrently with up to `workers` fibers and returns results in the SAME ORDER as the input array. Use index-tagged channels internally.
completion:
def parallel_map(items : Array(T), workers : Int32, &block : T -> R) : Array(R) forall T, R
  return [] of R if items.empty?

  jobs = Channel({Int32, T}).new(capacity: workers)
  output = Channel({Int32, R}).new(capacity: items.size)
  results = Array(R).new(items.size) { uninitialized R }

  workers.times do
    spawn do
      while (pair = jobs.receive?)
        idx, item = pair
        output.send({idx, block.call(item)})
      end
    end
  end

  spawn do
    items.each_with_index { |item, i| jobs.send({i, item}) }
    jobs.close
  end

  items.size.times do
    idx, value = output.receive
    results[idx] = value
  end

  results
end

class RateLimiter
  def initialize(per_second : Int32)
    @tokens = Channel(Nil).new(capacity: per_second)
    @stop_ch = Channel(Nil).new
    interval = 1.0 / per_second

    spawn do
      loop do
        select
        when @stop_ch.receive
          break
        else
          sleep interval.seconds
          select
          when @tokens.send(nil)
          else
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def acquire : Nil
    @tokens.receive
  end

  def stop : Nil
    @stop_ch.send(nil)
  end
end

def fan_in(*sources : Channel(T)) : Channel(T) forall T
  output = Channel(T).new(capacity: sources.size * 8)
  done = Channel(Nil).new

  sources.each do |src|
    spawn do
      while (v = src.receive?)
        output.send(v)
      end
      done.send(nil)
    end
  end

  spawn do
    sources.size.times { done.receive }
    output.close
  end

  output
end

prompt: Implement a generic `TypedStack(T)` backed by an Array. Provide `push`, `pop` (raises on empty), `peek` (raises on empty), `empty?`, and `size`. Include a `drain` method that yields each element top-to-bottom and leaves the stack empty.

class TypedStack(T)
  def initialize
    @data = [] of T
  end

  def push(item : T) : self
    @data << item
    self
  end

  def pop : T
    raise "stack is empty" if @data.empty?
    @data.pop
  end

  def peek : T
    raise "stack is empty" if @data.empty?
    @data.last
  end

  def empty? : Bool
    @data.empty?
  end

  def size : Int32
    @data.size
  end

  def drain(& : T ->) : Nil
    until @data.empty?
      yield @data.pop
    end
  end
end

    if yield item
      matches << item
    else
      rejects << item
    end
  end

  {matches: matches, rejects: rejects}

Raise a `ConfigLoader::ParseError` (custom, carries `line_number` and `raw_line`) on malformed lines. Use `ensure` to close the file handle even when an exception is raised.

class ConfigLoader
  class ParseError < Exception
    getter line_number : Int32
    getter raw_line : String

    def initialize(@line_number : Int32, @raw_line : String)
      super("Parse error on line #{@line_number}: #{@raw_line.inspect}")
    end
  end

  def self.load(path : String) : Hash(String, String)
    result = {} of String => String
    file = File.open(path)
    begin
      file.each_line.with_index(1) do |line, lineno|
        stripped = line.strip
        next if stripped.empty? || stripped.starts_with?('#')
        eq = stripped.index('=')
        raise ParseError.new(lineno, line) unless eq
        key = stripped[0...eq].strip
        raise ParseError.new(lineno, line) if key.empty?
        result[key] = stripped[(eq + 1)..].strip
      end
    ensure
      file.close
    end
    result
  end
end

prompt: Implement a generic `Result(T)` type in Crystal with two variants, `Ok(T)` and `Err`, where `Err` wraps an `Exception`. Add methods `ok? : Bool`, `err? : Bool`, `value! : T` (raises if Err), `error! : Exception` (raises if Ok), and `map(&block : T -> U) : Result(U) forall U` that propagates Err unchanged. Keep it self-contained.
completion:
abstract class Result(T)
  def ok? : Bool
    self.is_a?(Ok(T))
  end

  def err? : Bool
    self.is_a?(Err(T))
  end

  def value! : T
    raise "Called value! on an Err result" unless self.is_a?(Ok(T))
    self.value
  end

  def error! : Exception
    raise "Called error! on an Ok result" unless self.is_a?(Err(T))
    self.error
  end

  def map(&block : T -> U) : Result(U) forall U
    if self.is_a?(Ok(T))
      begin
        Ok(U).new(block.call(self.value))
      rescue ex
        Err(U).new(ex)
      end
    else
      Err(U).new(self.as(Err(T)).error)
    end
  end
end

class Ok(T) < Result(T)
  getter value : T

  def initialize(@value : T)
  end
end

class Err(T) < Result(T)
  getter error : Exception

  def initialize(@error : Exception)
  end
end

prompt: Build a `TokenScanner` class that scans a source string token by token. It should support three token kinds: `:number` (one or more digits), `:word` (one or more alpha chars), and `:symbol` (any single non-space char). `next_token` returns a `{kind: Symbol, value: String}` named tuple or `nil` at end-of-input. Skip whitespace between tokens.
completion:
class TokenScanner
  TOKEN_PATTERNS = [
    {:number, /\A\d+/},
    {:word, /\A[a-zA-Z]+/},
    {:symbol, /\A\S/},
  ]

  def initialize(source : String)
    @source = source
    @pos = 0
  end

  def next_token : NamedTuple(kind: Symbol, value: String)?
    skip_whitespace
    return nil if @pos >= @source.size

    remaining = @source[@pos..]
    TOKEN_PATTERNS.each do |kind, pattern|
      if m = remaining.match(pattern)
        @pos += m[0].size
        return {kind: kind, value: m[0]}
      end
    end

    nil
  end

  def tokens : Array(NamedTuple(kind: Symbol, value: String))
    result = [] of NamedTuple(kind: Symbol, value: String)
    while tok = next_token
      result << tok
    end
    result
  end

  private def skip_whitespace : Nil
    while @pos < @source.size && @source[@pos].ascii_whitespace?
      @pos += 1
    end
  end
end

prompt: Write a class `RateLimiter` that allows at most `limit` events within a rolling `window` (a `Time::Span`). Implement `allow? : Bool` which returns true and records the event timestamp when under the limit, or false when the limit is exceeded. Use monotonic instants internally for the window check so wall-clock adjustments cannot fool it.
completion:
class RateLimiter
  def initialize(@limit : Int32, @window : Time::Span)
    @events = Deque(Time::Instant).new
  end

  def allow? : Bool
    now = Time.instant
    purge_old(now)
    if @events.size < @limit
      @events << now
      true
    else
      false
    end
  end

  def remaining : Int32
    purge_old(Time.instant)
    (@limit - @events.size).clamp(0, @limit)
  end

  private def purge_old(now : Time::Instant) : Nil
    cutoff = now - @window
    while !@events.empty? && @events.first < cutoff
      @events.shift
    end
  end
end

  end

  def includes?(t : Time) : Bool
    t >= @start_time && t <= @end_time
  end

  def duration : Time::Span
    @end_time - @start_time

  def overlaps?(other : DateRange) : Bool
    @start_time <= other.end_time && other.start_time <= @end_time
  end

    day = @start_time.at_beginning_of_day
    last = @end_time.at_beginning_of_day
    while day <= last
      yield day
      day += 1.day
    end
  end
end
